abstract_ko: 생성형 AI의 등장은 글쓰기를 필자와 AI가 함께 의미를 구성하는 협력적 과정으로 전환시켰고, 기존의 과정 중심 글쓰기 모형(Flower & Hayes, 1981)은 이러한 AI 협력 글쓰기의 실제 인지 활동을 설명하는 데 더 이상 유효하지 않다. 이에 이 연구는 변화한 글쓰기의 인지 과정을 모형화하여 제안하고, 이를 바탕으로 AI 시대의 과정 중심 글쓰기 교육이 어떻게 재구성되어야 하는지 논의하는 데 목적을 두었다. 이를 위해, 대학생 필자 36명의 글쓰기 과정에서 수집된 즉시 회상 프로토콜을 질적으로 분석했다. 분석 결과 도출된 ‘AI 협력 글쓰기의 인지 과정 모형’은 다음의 특징을 가진다. 첫째, ‘과제 환경’은 기존에 없던 외부 정보 자원, 특히 AI가 산출하는 ‘AI 텍스트 후보군’을 포함하는 방향으로 확장되었고, ‘필자의 장기기억’은 기존 지식의 정교화와 함께 ‘AI 활용 지식’이 편입되는 방식으로 재구성되었다. 둘째, ‘쓰기 과정’은 AI의 실시간 개입을 전제로 ‘기획하기-생성하기-조정하기’로 재구조화되었으며, ‘기획하기’에는 텍스트 표상 구성, 목표·방향 설정, AI 개입 설계가, ‘생성하기’에는 내용 요소 생성, 표현·전개 다중 생성, 통합 구조 형성이, ‘조정하기’에는 텍스트 문제 탐지, 내용·구조 조정, 표현 정교화가 주요 인지 활동으로 포함되었다. 셋째, 필자의 텍스트 표상과 AI 제안을 지속적으로 대조하며 텍스트의 방향성과 표상을 조율하는 ‘이중 점검(dual monitoring)’이 AI 협력 글쓰기 과정을 통제하는 핵심적인 상위인지 메커니즘으로 제시되었다. 이를 토대로, 이 연구는 AI 시대의 과정 중심 글쓰기 교육이 새롭게 구성되어야 하는 방향을 제안했다. 특히, ‘기획하기-생성하기-조정하기’ 전 과정을 필자와 AI의 상호작용에 기반하여 다루고, 텍스트 표상과 AI 제안의 비교·판단을 수행하는 이중 점검 능력과 AI 활용 지식의 함양을 교육 내용의 중요한 축으로 설정해야 함을 강조했다.

title_ko: A Decade of Korean Research on AI-Mediated English Speaking: A Text-Mining Analysis
title_en: A Decade of Korean Research on AI-Mediated English Speaking: A Text-Mining Analysis
kw_en: artificial intelligence; English speaking; ChatGPT; chatbot; text mining; research trends
abstract_ko: This study examines abstract-level research trends in AI-mediated English-speaking education through a systematic text-mining analysis of English-language abstracts drawn from 130 Korean journal articles and theses published between 2015 and 2025. The dataset was constructed by retrieving English-language abstracts from RISS, a major Korean academic database and was analyzed using a combination of word-frequency analysis, TF-IDF weighting, N-gram extraction, and co-occurrence network analysis. These quantitative procedures were supplemented by topic modeling and CONCOR clustering to identify dominant thematic structures across the corpus. The results indicate that chatbot-based technologies—most notably PengTalk and ChatGPT—have emerged as the primary platforms for AI-mediated speaking practice, particularly within classroom-oriented instructional designs emphasizing proficiency development, level-based assessment, and feedback provision. Four major thematic domains were identified: classroom-based outcome validation, AI/chatbot-mediated support and proficiency gains, learner-centered task design and interaction, and speaker or user experience. Across these domains, AI is increasingly positioned not merely as an auxiliary tool but as an interactive learning partner that reshapes pedagogical practices and assessment approaches. The findings further suggest a growing emphasis on engagement, interactional authenticity, and formative feedback in AI-mediated speaking research. This study concludes by discussing implications for future classroom-embedded longitudinal research and the development of multimodal (speech–text) evaluation frameworks that foreground fairness, authenticity, and personalization in English-speaking assessment.

abstract_ko: The current study seeks to illuminate the roles of instructors in prior empirical research conducted in the domestic English education field. It systematically categorizes empirical studies on ChatGPT-based English instructions according to the main roles of instructors and suggests their frequency. In addition to analyzing these roles, further analysis of actual ChatGPT users, school levels, and outcome variables was necessary because these roles are closely tied to specific contexts. The study reviewed 76 previous studies that were conducted in South Korea between 2023 and 2024. These include 66 journal articles, nine master’s theses and one doctoral dissertation. The analysis identified five instructors’ roles: facilitators, technical supporters, resources of feedback, instructional organizers, and language instructors. Facilitators were the most common role found in studies of ChatGPT-based English instructions. Technical supporters, though relatively new, ranked as the second most frequent role. Resources of feedback focused on developing productive skills such as speaking and writing. Instructional organizers were primarily school teachers rather than university faculty. Language instructors emphasized grammar even when teaching other written language skills. These findings are expected to give comprehensive educational implications and insights into instructors’ roles when utilizing ChatGPT for English language learning in the Korean EFL context.

title_ko: Analyzing the Needs for Korean EFL Students’ AI Competency by their Perception and Actual Use of AI-Utilized Tools

abstract_ko: The purpose of this study is to figure out the educational needs for Korean college students’ competency of AI use, based upon the differences in their perceived importance and actual performance of AI-utilized tools in the classroom. To accomplish this research purpose, it specifically aims to uncover 1) How important did Korean college students perceive the use of AI tools for their English learning? 2) How much did the students perceive that they actually use AI tools for their English learning? 3) What are the most urgent educational needs regarding English learning competencies for using AI in the classroom? Fifty students responded to the IPA survey, and the collected data were analyzed by using IPA and the Borich needs analysis. The analytical results suggested that 1) learners have already secured basic skills in using AI tools and interacting with AI in English learning, 2) they have a significant educational need for higher-order competencies regarding critical evaluation of AI-generated output and strategic modification based on AI-provided feedback. Lastly, pedagogical implications and suggestions for the AI-assisted language instruction were also discussed.

abstract_ko: The Ministry of Education in Korea has officially approved the implementation of the Artificial Intelligence Digital Textbook (AIDT) in schools, which integrates adaptive learning and automated evaluation systems. This study examines the usefulness of the AI feedback system within AIDT from the perspective of English teachers. The AIDT’s AI feedback system aims to support teachers’ assessment practices by providing individualized feedback for students with developing writing skills. However, how the system influences teachers’ assessment practices remains unclear. This study investigated the experiences of four Korean middle school English teachers using the AI feedback system and identified the affordances and constraints that emerged during use. Teachers assessed sample student essays using the system; their online assessment sessions were recorded and followed by in-depth interviews. Based on these experiences, teachers suggested practical improvements to enhance the feedback quality and system usability. This study offers insights into how teachers incorporate AI feedback into classroom assessment and proposes directions for refining the AI feedback system.

abstract_ko: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into educational contexts has raised pressing questions about how writing processes and learner agency are reconfigured in AI-mediated environments. This study examines how Korean preservice English as a foreign language (EFL) teachers engaged with GenAI during a narrative writing task and how AI mediation functioned across stages of composing. Fourteen senior-level preservice teachers completed a take-home narrative writing task that permitted GenAI use, accompanied by process journals. A qualitative thematic analysis revealed that GenAI was used primarily as a mediational resource rather than as an autonomous text generator, with its role shifting from idea generation and meaning negotiation in early drafting to linguistic refinement during later revision. Participants demonstrated differentiated patterns of agency, ranging from dialogic and evaluative engagement with AI output to minimally mediated use characterized by uncritical adoption. The findings suggest that AI-supported writing is best understood as a process-based and dialogic activity in which educational value depends on how writers regulate and interpret AI support. The study discusses theoretical and pedagogical implications for preservice teacher education in AI-rich writing contexts.

abstract_ko: The present study examines how accurately Korean EFL teachers identify the authorship of English essays as student-written or AI-generated and explores the criteria they employ in making these judgments. It further investigates whether teachers’ perceptions of authorship influence their assessment of writing quality. The participants were 78 Korean EFL pre-service and in-service teachers, who evaluated a total of 12 essays for both authorship identification and writing quality. The results showed that teachers’ overall authorship identification accuracy was approximately 58%, only slightly above chance level, despite their relatively high level of confidence (7.13 out of 10 points). Teachers tended to associate student-written texts with limited idea development, personal and experience-based examples, and a limited vocabulary and syntactic variation, while attributing well-developed and information-rich ideas, consistent but formulaic organization, generalized content, and sophisticated vocabulary use to AI-generated texts. In addition, teachers’ perceptions of AI involvement were found to significantly influence their writing assessments. Given the limited reliability of authorship identification and the influence of perceived authorship on writing assessment, the study suggests a need to revise assessment rubrics to foreground writing process, idea development, and learner agency, while incorporating AI as a pedagogical scaffold in L2 writing instruction.

abstract_ko: As generative AI is increasingly being used for real-time interaction, existing SLA theories—notably Complex Dynamic Systems Theory (CDST)—face limitations in explaining the micro-mechanisms of how meaning is constructed and negotiated through language in real-time human–AI interactions. Adopting an abductive approach, this study proposes the Quantum Model of Language (QMoL) to reconceptualize language as probabilistic meaning potentials that collapse into specific form-meaning combinations through contextualized interaction. Grounded in research findings in quantum cognition, QMoL defines language use and acquisition as a cyclical process involving meaning-wave generation, contextual collapse, particle-like realization, and reintegration into the learner’s semantic field. This framework provides a parsimonious explanation for linguistic complexity, variability, creativity, and context sensitivity through the unified quantum concepts of superposition, collapse, decoherence, and entanglement. Pedagogically, the study proposes a paradigm shift from knowledge transmission to AI-enhanced prompt engineering and coaching. In this model, AI functions as a dynamic resonance field while teachers act as coaches guiding learners to exercise their agency in orchestrating their own meaning-construction processes during interaction. Implications are discussed for establishing QMoL as a coherent theoretical model for fostering learner agency, adaptive fluency, and human-centered communication in AI-mediated second language education.

abstract_ko: This study explores the educational convergence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and the metaverse in a university- level English course, with the aim of enhancing students’ understanding of English-speaking cultures and their digital literacy. A 16-week course was designed and implemented, in which 30 undergraduate students collaboratively developed English cultural content using generative AI tools (e.g., Vrew, Napkin AI, Hedra AI) and constructed immersive cultural spaces within a metaverse platform. Employing a case study approach, data were collected through a post-course survey and open-ended reflections. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative responses were examined through thematic analysis. The results indicate that the course significantly promoted students’ intercultural understanding, particularly in recognizing cultural diversity and developing empathetic perspectives toward people from different cultural backgrounds. In addition, students reported high levels of confidence in using digital technologies, including real-time collaboration in the metaverse and creative multimedia content production with AI tools. Qualitative findings further revealed that learners perceived generative AI not as a substitute for learning, but as a collaborative tool that supported planning, visualization, and creative expression. Overall course satisfaction was also notably high, reflecting strong learner engagement and ownership. Based on these findings, the study highlights the pedagogical value of integrating generative AI and the metaverse in English education and suggests the importance of critical digital literacy to support effective and ethical technology use in higher education contexts.

abstract_ko: This study investigates adult EFL learners’ perceptions of AI-supported repetition in functional English instruction, focusing on how repetition is experienced and interpreted within AI-mediated learning tasks. Drawing on qualitative data from open-ended questionnaires and AI-generated task outputs, the study analyzes learners’ reflections on reinforcement and its perceived impact on learning and confidence. Findings indicate that learners view AI-supported repetition as meaningful and confidence-enhancing rather than mechanical. Participants report that repeated engagement with AI-generated language supports the internalization of professional discourse patterns and reduces language-related anxiety. Learners describe using AI output as a reference point to confirm expression choices, increase familiarity with functional language, and prepare for oral performance, while also demonstrating awareness of potential overreliance or uncritical copying. The study concludes that when repetition is adaptive, contextualized, and critically mediated, AI-assisted learning can foster perceived procedural fluency and learner autonomy, offering a pedagogically sustainable model for adult functional English instruction. By foregrounding learner perceptions, the study reframes AI-mediated repetition as an adaptive and reflective process shaped by learner agency rather than as mechanical practice.

title_en: Investigating the Use of AI Chatbots to Enhance EFL Young Learners’ Achievement, Self-Directed Learning, and Willingness to Communicate

abstract_ko: <abstract lang="english">Given the growing interest in AI technology, its potential to provide interactive language environments for young EFL learners has gained increasing attention. This study investigates the effects of using AI chatbots on English achievement, self-directed learning readiness, and willingness to communicate among primary school students in Korea. 49 fifth-grade students participated, divided into an experimental group (n = 25) and a control group (n = 24). The experimental group engaged in English lessons incorporating interactive and communicative activities utilizing two types of AI chatbots—Replika and ChatGPT—for 14 sessions over one semester, while the control group participated in traditional classroom activities. The data were analyzed using ANCOVA to examine the differences between the groups. The results revealed that while there was no statistically significant difference in English achievement, the experimental group showed significant improvements in self-directed learning readiness and willingness to communicate compared to the control group. Qualitative findings further indicated that the students perceived chatbots as non-judgmental conversation partners, which helped reduce anxiety and encouraged voluntary learning interactions. Despite some technical challenges reported, the findings suggest that AI chatbots have significant potential as educational tools to enhance the affective domain and self-directed learning autonomy of young EFL learners.

title_en: From Tool Overload to Instructional Alignment: Developing Pre-Service Teachers’ Digital and AI Teaching Competence
kw_en: EdTech; generative AI; microteaching; instructional alignment; rehearsal-based feedback
abstract_ko: <abstract lang="english">This qualitative case study investigates how EdTech and generative AI were integrated into English microteaching to develop pre-service teachers’ digital and AI teaching competencies, with particular attention to instructional alignment among learning goals, activities, and assessment. The study was conducted in an elective teacher-education course titled “Digital·AI Teaching Competency Development,” redesigned from a conventional microteaching practicum. Nineteen pre-service English teachers designed and delivered English-medium microteaching lessons incorporating EdTech and generative AI, participated in rehearsal-based feedback sessions, and completed reflective journals and semi-structured interviews. Data included lesson plans, teaching artifacts, recorded lessons, reflections, and interview transcripts. Qualitative coding and cross-case comparison identified three findings. First, generative AI functioned primarily as linguistic and structural scaffolding during preparation. Second, tools such as Padlet and Kahoot were selected in the enactment phase because they supported learner participation and formative assessment. Third, rehearsal-based feedback corrected tool-centered designs and restored alignment among learning goals, communicative tasks, and assessment. The findings suggest that the educational value of digital tools depends not on the number of technologies used but on their contribution to coherent instructional design. Implications are discussed for practice-based teacher education that emphasizes alignment-oriented planning and iterative feedback cycles.

abstract_ko: This paper reconceptualizes Speech-to-Speech (STS) systems for English conversation education through a modular pipeline lens. We argue that educational effectiveness depends on intentionally designing the VAD–STT–LLM–TTS pipeline as an integrated pedagogical system rather than treating STS as a black box. We summarize the functional roles of each component and examine how they shape key dimensions of conversation learning, including fluency, accuracy, interactional competence, affective support, and pronunciation/listening development. We also highlight cross-module dynamics such as error propagation and compensation and discuss how end-to-end latency influences learners’ sense of real-time interaction. Based on these insights, we propose practical design principles for classroom and self-study contexts, including task- and proficiency-sensitive VAD/STT settings, level-adaptive LLM prompting and feedback strategies, and activity designs leveraging controllable TTS for listen-and-repeat, shadowing, and role-play. We conclude with implications for future empirical validation and learner- and domain-specific optimization.

title_en: Critical Reading and Multimodal Composing through ChatGPT in the First-Year English Literature Classroom
kw_en: AI pedagogy; “A Scandal in Bohemia”; multimodal literacy; prompting; intermedial practice
abstract_ko: This essay offers a case study of the experience of teaching first-year English major students Arthur Conan Doyle’s “A Scandal in Bohemia” by integrating ChatGPT into a literature exercise. One of the course’s weekly assignments asked the students (all English majors, mostly freshmen) to convert Irene Adler’s letter that appears in the ending of the short story into six-panel comic strips by writing a specific set of prompts into ChatGPT and editing the resulting images. Investigating six assignment samples whose engagement with the chatbot demonstrates each student’s different understanding of and creative relationship with the tool, the essay suggests that with the help of ChatGPT’s multimodal function to draw illustrations the students ventured into creative terrain where they could reimagine Doyle’s source story. This intermedial exercise also underlines the role of prompts, which are becoming a new writing genre. Ultimately, AI technology calls for a reconsideration of pedagogical practices and goals to utilize prompt technologies as a new writing mode for the so-called digital natives in English classes.

title_en: Research on the Validity of AI-based Assessment of English Essays and Probing Measurement Outcomes of Specific Scoring Dimensions
kw_en: latest models of ChatGPT; AI-based essay scoring; validation of scoring results; dimension-specific scoring; AI-based qualitative feedback
abstract_ko: This study compared the performance of three ChatGPT versions, 4.1, 5, and the latest 5.2 in evaluating EFL college students’ English essays. It also examined the validity of AI-based automated scoring by comparing the results with those of expert raters. Comparisons were conducted from both quantitative and qualitative perspectives. This study is significant in that, following earlier validation studies of initial ChatGPT models, it investigates the most recent models to date. In addition, it explores AI-based scoring outcomes across distinct components of an analytic rubric, such as content, vocabulary, and grammar, thereby extending prior research to domain-specific scoring dimensions. Quantitative findings showed that ChatGPT-4.1 performed similarly to the 5.2 model, whereas ChatGPT-5 produced contrasting scoring outcomes. Overall, the 5.2 model yielded results most closely aligned with expert ratings. In the domain-level analyses, the three models produced different rating patterns in areas requiring deep content understanding and logical organization. This suggests that concerns raised in pre-AI automated scoring research remain relevant and warrant continued attention and investigation. Differences among the three versions were also evident in the qualitative descriptive feedback. The newest model, 5.2, provided the most detailed and practically useful feedback, highlighting its relative advantage in feedback quality. The paper concludes with suggestions for many future research avenues based on the limitations of the current study.

abstract_ko: 본 연구는 한국어 논술형 에세이 자동채점(AES)에서 문장 단위 임베딩을 문서 수준으로 집계하는 방식에 따라 예측 성능과 문장 정보 활용 양상이 어떻게 달라지는지를 분석하는 것을 목적으로 하였다. 이를 위하여 문장 임베딩을 비학습적으로 통합하는 단순 풀링 기반 집계 방식(Mean, Max, Min Pooling)과 문장 단위 중요도를 학습적으로 산출하는 Attention 기반 집계 방식(Gated MIL Attention, TransMIL Attention)을 적용하여 성능을 비교하였다. 분석 결과, 단순 풀링 방식은 일정 수준의 예측 성능을 보였으나 Attention 기반 집계 방식과 비교할 때 성능 지표 전반에서 뚜렷한 우위를 보이지는 않았다. 반면 Gated MIL Attention과 TransMIL Attention은 일부 성능 지표에서 상대적으로 우수한 결과를 나타냈으며, 문장 단위 정보가 동일하게 처리되기보다 가중화되거나 문장 간 관계적 맥락 속에서 활용될 수 있음을 시사하였다. 특히 Attention 기반 집계 구조를 분석한 결과, 상대적으로 높은 가중치를 부여받은 문장들이 주장 및 근거 제시와 같은 논설문 핵심 기능을 수행하는 문장들로 나타나, 문장 중요도 정보가 점수 예측뿐 아니라 에세이 구조 해석에도 활용될 수 있음을 확인하였다. 다만 본 연구는 문장 간 Attention 관계를 탐색적으로 분석한 것으로, 개별 문장의 의미적 기능이나 평가 기준과의 직접적인 대응 관계를 정량적으로 규명하는 데에는 한계가 있다. 또한 채점자 식별 정보의 부재로 인해 채점자 간 일치도 산출이나 채점자별 편차를 고려한 분석은 수행하지 못하였다. 그럼에도 불구하고 본 연구는 문장 단위 정보를 고려하는 Attention 기반 집계 구조가 AES에서 구조적으로 의미 있는 접근임을 실증적으로 제시하였다는 점에서 의의를 갖는다. 향후 연구에서는 채점자 정보가 포함된 데이터셋과 다양한 논술 유형을 활용하여 Attention 기반 집계 구조의 타당성과 일반화 가능성을 추가로 검증할 필요가 있다.

abstract_ko: This study examines the impact of generative artificial intelligence (AI) on the English writing of Korean university students. Using activity theory as a framework, the researcher examined the writing strategies and outcomes of two groups of students: those with high English proficiency and those with average English proficiency. Adopting a qualitative case study design, the study engaged ten undergraduates from two leading Korean universities. Data were collected through interviews and essay-writing tasks, and the essays were evaluated for originality, coherence, and critical ability. The results reveal that AI tools boosted students’ confidence and efficiency in writing. However, proficiency differences shaped outcomes: high-proficiency students tended to critically evaluate AI’s suggestions, while average-proficiency students often relied on AI uncritically. Across both groups, AI enhanced fluency and grammatical accuracy but showed limitations in fostering originality. Pedagogically, the findings suggest that AI should be incorporated into English writing instruction in ways that promote critical AI literacy and emphasize human agency in writing. The study is limited by its small sample size, which restricts generalizability. Future research should expand to include larger and more diverse student populations, and compare the impact of different AI platforms (e.g., Grammarly, Gemini, and ChatGPT).

abstract_ko: 본 연구의 목적은 도입 초기 단계인 AI 디지털교과서를 직접 활용한 중등교사들의 경험과 의견을 분석하고, 향후 AI 디지털교과서의 개선방안을 도출하는 데 있다. 이를 위하여 본인의 수업에서 AI 디지털교과서를 직접 활용한 경험이 있는 6명의 수학, 영어, 정보 교사들을 대상으로 AI 디지털교과서 활용 과정과 환경을 깊이 있게 탐색할 수 있는 반구조화된 질문지를 구성하여 서면 인터뷰와 심층 인터뷰를 진행하였다. 심층 인터뷰 결과는 질적 연구방법인 반복적 비교분석법을 활용하여 중등교사들의 AI 디지털교과서 활용 경험을 범주별로 분류하였다. 범주는 크게 시스템 및 인터페이스, 콘텐츠, 수업 운영 및 관리, 인프라 및 제반시설 등 4개의 범주와 16개 하위 내용을 도출하였다. 연구 결과, 교사들의 AI 디지털교과서 활용 경험을 범주별로 분류하여 살펴봄으로써 AI 디지털교과서의 공통적 경험과 교과별 특성을 파악할 수 있었고, AI 디지털교과서의 개선방안도 도출할 수 있었다. AI 디지털교과서에 대한 주요 개선방안은 공통으로 인터페이스의 단순화, 수업 재구성 기능 강화, 제반 환경 제공 필요, 교과별로는 다양한 콘텐츠 제공(수학), 교내 AI 디지털교과서 통합 관리자 지정(영어), 채점기능 강화(정보) 등을 들 수 있다. 본 연구를 통해 도입 초기 AI 디지털교과서를 활용한 교사 경험을 탐색해봄으로써 앞으로 AI 디지털교과서의 지속적 개선의 토대가 되길 기대한다.

abstract_ko: AI 기반 글쓰기 교육에 관한 선행연구는 주로 생성형 AI의 도구적 활용에 초점을 맞추고 있다. 본 연구의 목적은 학습자가 데이터를 근거로 탐구하고 글쓰기 과정에서 AI를 비판적으로 활용하며 자신의 글을 성찰할 수 있도록 지원하는 데이터 기반 AI 융합 글쓰기 수업 모형과 설계 원리를 개발하고 타당화하는 것이다. 설계․개발 연구방법론의 유형 2 모형 연구 방법을 활용해 선행연구 분석, 2회에 걸친 내적 타당화 검토 이후 도출된 모형을 4개의 집단(학교)에서 외적 타당화를 수행하여 총 437명의 중․고등학생을 대상으로 수업을 실행하였다. 본 연구에서 개발된 모형은 5E 탐구 순환 모형(Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate)을 기반으로 단계별 활동을 구조화하고 AI 기반 도구가 통합되도록 설계했다. 또한, 핵심 질문 탐구, 맥락적 데이터 탐색, 데이터 분석, 비판적 비교, AI 지원 스캐폴딩, 통합 데이터 관리, 순차적 AI 도구 통합, 표현 및 공유, 윤리적 AI 실천, 메타인지적 개인화의 10가지 설계 원리를 도출하였다. 현장 적용 결과 학습자의 AI 리터러시와 글쓰기 효능감에서의 유의미한 향상을 확인할 수 있었다. 본 연구는 AI를 사고 확장, 데이터 기반 논증, 메타인지적 성찰을 지원하는 인지적 조력자로 설정하여, AI 리터러시와 글쓰기 역량을 통합적으로 함양하는 수업 모형을 제시하였다는 데 의의가 있다.

abstract_ko: 본 연구는 EFL 학습자가 영어 글쓰기를 수행할 때 ChatGPT와 어떤 단계적 상호작용 패턴을 보이는지, ChatGPT 피드백 통합 수준에 따라 그 양상이 어떻게 달라지는지를 탐색하고자 한다. 서울 소재 4년제 대학 학부생 13명을 대상으로 “온라인 학습은 오프라인 학습보다 더 효과적이다”라는 주제의 글쓰기를 ChatGPT만을 활용해 수행하도록 하였다. 상호작용 로그는 Guo와 Li(2024)의 4단계 글쓰기 모형(준비-편집-교정-성찰)을 기반으로, 하위 단계인 아이디어 생성, 아이디어 구성, 논리적 전개, 근거 활용, 글쓰기 스타일 교정, 오류 수정, 글 평가의 7개 범주로 코딩하였다. 담화 단위별 ChatGPT 피드백 반영 정도를 ‘직접 반영-수정 후 반영-미반영’으로 코딩하여 통합 점수를 산출하고, 상대적 순위를 기준으로 고통합(7명)과 저통합(6명) 집단으로 나누어 순서화된 네트워크 분석(Ordered Network Analysis, ONA)을 통해 단계 간 전이 구조를 시각화․정량 분석하였다. 전체 네트워크에서는 ‘글쓰기 스타일 교정’과 ‘근거 활용’이 중심 허브로 작동하며, ‘글쓰기 스타일 교정 → 아이디어 생성 → 근거 활용 → 글쓰기 스타일 교정’으로 이어지는 순환적 전이 패턴이 나타났다. 또한, 고통합 그룹에서 ‘글쓰기 스타일 교정’, ‘근거 활용’, ‘논리적 전개’ 간 전이가 두드러졌고, 저통합 그룹에서는 ‘아이디어 생성/구성’, ‘근거 활용’, ‘오류 수정’ 중심의 전이가 강조되는 경향이 나타났다. 이는 ChatGPT가 EFL 학습자의 글쓰기 과정에서 주로 언어적 표현 조정과 근거 활용을 중심으로 활용되는 경향이 있음을 보여주며, 일부 학습자에게서는 아이디어 재검토와 논리 조정으로 확장될 수 있음을 시사한다. 이러한 결과는 AI 기반 글쓰기 지원의 활용 범위와 교수 설계 방향을 논의하기 위한 기초적 시사점을 제공한다.

abstract_ko: This study examines the impact of an inquiry-based English reading program using ChatGPT on elementary learners’ reading proficiency and perceptions. Conducted over four weeks with 5th-grade students, the study employed a mixed-methods approach combining pre- and post-tests with post-interviews. Results revealed significant improvement in learners' reading abilities, particularly in contextual understanding and inference-making. ChatGPT interactions boosted learners’ confidence, reduced anxiety, and fostered autonomy and metacognitive strategies. However, differentiated scaffolding was needed to accommodate varying levels of digital literacy and language proficiency. While AI acted as a motivating learning partner, effective integration required tailored prompts and leveled reading materials. This study may provide a practical framework for integrating AI into primary English education and could contribute to redefining the roles of teachers, learners, and technology in future classrooms.

abstract_ko: This study conducts a narrative review of domestic empirical literature of the past decade to explore the current state and future directions of AIEE for primary learners. Utilizing a multi-dimensional coding framework, the research analyzes 103 studies in terms of general research, educational, and implicational contexts. The findings reveal a chronological evolution categorized into three phases ranging from early inception to recent accelerated growth driven by generative technologies and digital policies. Methodologically, the result demonstrates a strong preference for mixed methods and quantitative approaches, focusing on verifying educational impacts and efficacy. Regarding educational context, AI applications have predominantly focused on productive skills, particularly speaking and writing, while consistently yielding significant positive impacts on the affective domain by reducing anxiety and increasing learners' willingness to communicate. The study further highlights a transition toward blended and flipped learning models that integrate commercial platforms and recent generative AI tools. Consequently, we demonstrate through our results underscore the impending normalization of AI-assisted language learning(AIALL), necessitating a paradigm shift in the teacher’s role from a primary linguistic source to a facilitator and coach.

abstract_ko: As generative AI is increasingly integrated into education, the need to develop learners' ability to critically evaluate and self-directly revise AI-based texts is growing. Accordingly, this present study aims to establish a learner-driven revision model based on digital critical thinking. To this end, oral presentation scripts written by Korean university EFL learners were analyzed to examine the frequency, functional distribution, and lexical concentration of discourse connectives. A learner corpus (KULC) was constructed based on presentation scripts (totaling 21,203 tokens) written by 84 nursing and health science students on major-related topics in 2021, before the widespread adoption of AI-based writing tools. Discourse connectives were classified into additive, adversative, causal, and sequential connectives according to the classification system of Larsen-Freeman and Celce-Murcia (2015) and extracted using AntConc. The analysis results showed that discourse connectives in the additive and sequential categories were most frequently used, particularly high-frequency expressions such as "and," "also," "first," and "second." Conversely, adversative and causal connectives were used less frequently, and lexical diversity was limited due to a reliance on specific expressions such as "but" and "therefore." Based on these results, this study proposed a rubric to promote balanced use of discourse connectives across functional categories. Ultimately, this rubric will help learners evaluate and refine their AI-assisted presentation scripts independently. This self-directed process will strengthen both discourse cohesion and rhetorical clarity, leading to a much more effective presentation delivery.

abstract_ko: Despite growing interest in AI adoption in higher education, limited research has examined how university students conceptualize the pedagogical meaning of AI beyond measures of attitudes and user satisfaction. This study explored how Korean university students conceptualized AI in English education through analysis of 40 reflective essays and 80 peer feedback comments collected across four instructional contexts. Qualitative thematic and constant comparative analysis identified four recurrent perspectives: AI as an efficiency tool, a source of risk or limitation, a catalyst for pedagogical reconfiguration, and a vision for future English education. While all perspectives appeared across contexts, their relative emphasis varied by instructional role. Students writing as learners focused on efficiency and risk; those considering policy stressed ethical guidelines; and those positioned as prospective teachers proposed practical classroom and materials design strategies. Peer feedback supported conceptual development by encouraging critical reflection and refinement of pedagogically actionable ideas. Overall, the findings suggest that students view AI not merely as a technical aid but as a pedagogical agent connected to autonomy, ethics, assessment, and teacher–learner dynamics, highlighting the need for instructional designs that foster AI literacy through guided reflection and peer feedback.

abstract_ko: This study examined the effects of integrating ChatGPT into college English classes over one semester, focusing on changes in students’ perceptions of ChatGPT, language anxiety, and self-regulated learning strategies, as well as the relationships among these variables after integration. Thirty-seven first-year students participated in ChatGPT-supported reading and writing courses. From Weeks 3 to 13, students used ChatGPT to explore vocabulary meanings, construct sentences using newly learned expressions, and engage in text-based discussions on weekly topics. Pre-post questionnaires were administered, consisting of three sections: (1) English learning anxiety, (2) self-regulated learning, and (3) perceptions of ChatGPT. Adopting a pre-post questionnaire design, the study employed paired-samples t-tests and correlation analyses to assess changes and associations among the variables. The findings showed that students developed more positive attitudes toward ChatGPT as a language learning tool. Correlation analyses indicated strong to moderate within-domain relationships after ChatGPT use, whereas cross-domain correlations were relatively weak. These results underscore the need for explicit pedagogical guidance to reduce language anxiety and strengthen self-regulated learning in L2 contexts.

abstract_ko: This purpose of the study is to examine the effect of AI-based English presentation learning activities on students’ metacognitive strategies. A total of 60 first-year students enrolled at D University in Chungcheong Province engaged in English presentation tasks using AI-based learning activities. The students used AI in the process of preparing for English presentations and completed four English presentation tasks. For the study, pre- and post-surveys related to metacognitive strategies and two English presentation tests were administered. The results indicated that learners’ English presentation ability improved after participating in AI-based learning activities. Overall metacognitive strategy use showed a significant increase with significant gains in planning, monitoring, and evaluating strategies, but not in problem-solving. Students also reported positive experiences, noting improvements in pronunciation accuracy, tone, speaking fluency, and confidence, as well as increased opportunities for independent learning. However, some concerns were raised regarding the reliability of AI feedback and the unnatural pronunciation or intonation compared to native speakers. These findings suggest that integrating ChatGPT into TBLT can effectively enhance writing performance and foster positive professional perceptions among preservice teachers. This study provides empirical support for incorporating GAI into English teacher education and offers practical implications for designing effective GAI-integrated writing pedagogy in teacher education contexts.

abstract_ko: This study examines two AI-driven written feedback tools—ChatGPT and AI Digital Textbooks (AIDT)—by comparing their effects on Korean middle school students’ English writing performance and perceptions. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected from 31 teachers through surveys and five semi-structured interviews. Most participants reported moderate to high levels of familiarity with ChatGPT and recognized its value for lesson planning and grammar support. However, they also expressed concerns about plagiarism, student overreliance, and the potential weakening of critical thinking skills. These perspectives were shaped by Thailand’s exam-oriented education system and persistent digital inequality. Overall, the findings indicate that effective AI adoption in Thai EFL classrooms requires not only pedagogical readiness but also policy coherence and infrastructural equity.

abstract_ko: This study examines the developmental trajectory of feedback research in Korean EFL writing from the early 1990s to 2025 through a qualitative systematic synthesis of KCI-indexed journal articles. Drawing on major learning theories and educational reforms, the study identifies four stages that reflect shifts in curriculum policy, assessment practices, and the gradual incorporation of digital and AI-based tools. Early work was characterized by teacher-centered and form-focused corrective feedback, followed by comparative studies of feedback types influenced by sociocultural theory and formative assessment perspectives. Recent research has increasingly addressed learners’ metacognition, self-regulation, feedback uptake, and AI-mediated practices. Despite these broader theoretical orientations, the literature remains dominated by short-term interventions and perception-based studies, with limited evidence on sustained writing development in classroom settings. The findings indicate a gap between theoretical advancement and instructional practice in Korean EFL writing. This study calls for longitudinal, classroom-based, and mixed-method research that examines how teacher-, peer-, and AI-mediated feedback can be integrated within context-sensitive instructional models.

abstract_ko: The rapid proliferation of Generative AI (GenAI) in higher education has introduced significant benefits but also caused widespread cognitive offloading, potentially eroding learner agency. As an exploratory study utilizing a small-scale sample (N=23), this research investigates the impact of an AI-restricted English discussion environment on university students’ self-directed learning (SDL) and their perceptions of critical agency and course satisfaction. Employing a 10-week intervention that prohibited AI access during spontaneous communication, the study sought to enforce cognitive onloading and pushed output. Paired-samples t-tests revealed statistically significant improvements across all five SDL sub-factors, most notably in autonomy (t=-9.23) and self-concept (t=-8.19). These results confirm that AI restriction functions as a desirable difficulty, compelling students to navigate the struggles of lexical/syntactic formulation during discussion. Qualitative analysis further revealed that learners viewed the restriction as a necessary pedagogical measure for fostering critical thinking skills (82.6% positive). Furthermore, 86.9% of participants expressed a desire for future AI-restricted courses. These findings advocate for a ‘strategic hybrid model’ in university curricula, where ‘AI-free zones’ are intentionally designated during production phases to reclaim cognitive agency and foster intrinsic motivation.

abstract_ko: Traditionally, teaching history of English often relies on lecture-based explanations of linguistic change, which limits learners’ opportunities to experience language within its historical and sociocultural contexts. This study explores the pedagogical potential of integrating metaverse and generative AI chatbot technology into teaching history of English. To this end, this study explores the experiences of 37 undergraduate students working on the creation of metaverse spaces with AI chatbots introducing the crucial events, figures and linguistic features according to the development of English. Through an in-depth analysis of its results and students’ reflective reports, this study reveals that students transformed historical timelines into immersive spatial designs and used chatbots as instructional mediators (e.g., historical figures, quiz guides, or language-change explainers). The project fostered digital, prompt, and design literacies and shifted English history learning from memorization toward contextualized, meaning-oriented understanding. The findings suggest that combining metaverse environments with generative AI can effectively support experiential and creative approaches to History of English education.

abstract_ko: This study examined differences between ChatGPT and native English-speaking teachers in erroranalysis and writing assessment of English learner compositions, and explored the relationshipbetween error analysis and assessment outcomes. Twenty-seven college English learnersparticipated in the study, and Pearson correlation, multiple regression analysis, and one-wayANOVA were conducted. The results showed that ChatGPT and the teachers shared a broadlysimilar framework for recognizing learner errors, but differed in the scope and focus of erroridentification. While both displayed comparable tendencies in ‘language-use’ errors, ChatGPTidentified a greater number of errors in ‘content’, ‘organization’, and ‘vocabulary’ based onbroader, macro-level criteria, whereas the teachers identified more errors in ‘writing technique’. Inwriting assessment, no significant differences were found in surface-level linguistic domains;however, a significant difference emerged between ChatGPT and one native English teacher in‘content’ and ‘organization’. Finally, error frequency was not applied as a uniform penalty factorby either ChatGPT and the teachers, suggesting that assessment outcomes depended more on howevaluators interpreted and incorporated errors within their evaluative perspectives. Pedagogicalimplications and directions of further research were discussed.

abstract_ko: This study investigates elementary pre-service English teachers’ perceptions of educationaltechnology (EduTech) in microteaching contexts, focusing on its perceived impact on teachingefficacy, lesson satisfaction, and future instructional intentions. 35 members among the pre-serviceteachers who enrolled in a teacher education program conducted English microteaching lessonsincorporating diverse EduTech tools are the participants of this study. Data were collected throughpost-microteaching surveys and reflective journals and analyzed using mixed methods. Quantitative results indicated highly positive perceptions across all domains, with particularlystrong ratings for instructional effectiveness and intentions for future integration. Teaching efficacyand lesson satisfaction were also positively evaluated, with high internal consistency across items. Qualitative analysis revealed that participants perceived EduTech as a supportive instructionalresource rather than a substitute for the teacher, emphasizing its role in enhancing learnermotivation, classroom interaction, and formative feedback. The findings highlight the need forsystematic, practice-based EduTech training within pre-service teacher education to promotemeaningful and confident integration of technology into elementary English classrooms.

title_ko: The Role of Model Prompts and Feedback Seeking Behavior in ChatGPT-Assisted EFL Writing
title_en: The Role of Model Prompts and Feedback Seeking Behavior in ChatGPT-Assisted EFL Writing
kw_en: generative artificial intelligence; L2 writing; prompt design; corrective feedback; feedback seeking behavior
abstract_ko: The increasing use of generative AI (Gen-AI) tools in education is attracting scholarly attention, particularly regarding their impact on second language (L2) writing development. While Gen-AI provides cognitive and motivational support, concerns persist about overreliance and diminished learner autonomy. This study examines how prompt design affects the quality of AI-assisted writing revisions and learners’ feedback seeking behavior (FSB), which serves as an indicator of learner agency. Forty-three undergraduate EFL students were randomly assigned to one of two conditions: a direct feedback model prompt (DMP) or an indirect feedback model prompt (IMP). After writing initial drafts independently, participants revised their work using ChatGPT. The results indicated significant improvement within-group, especially in language use and vocabulary. Although there were no statistically significant differences in revised-draft scores between the groups, the DMP group performed better in mechanics and language use, with small to moderate effect sizes. Regarding FSB, while group differences were not statistically significant, effect size analysis showed that the DMP group was more engaged in seeking feedback. These findings suggest that prompt design can influence learner-AI interactions and enhance learner agency, providing valuable insights for integrating Gen-AI tools into L2 writing instruction.
